answers.answer: Since $\overline{XY}\parallel\overline{AD}$, $m(\angle CXY)=m(\angle CAD)$ (corresponding angles). In the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, $m(\angle CAD)=m(\angle CBD)$ (both on base CD, same side). So $m(\angle CXY)=m(\angle CBY)$, i.e. $m(\angle YXC)=m(\angle YBC)$. These are two angles on the base YC, in the same direction of it, so BXYC is a cyclic quadrilateral. This answer is based on the standard figure, which I couldn't see.

From the First part, BXYC is cyclic. $\angle XBY$ and $\angle XCY$ are drawn on the same base XY and in the same direction of it, and both are inscribed in the circle through B, X, Y, C. So $m(\angle XBY)=m(\angle XCY)$. This answer is based on the standard figure, which I couldn't see.
